newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus bars U.S. Soros Foundation representative.
newsitem.headline: Belarus bars U.S. Soros Foundation representative.

text.p: Belarussian authorities have barred the executive director of the Soros Foundation from re-entering the country and accused him of supporting the opposition, state-run television said on Monday.
The foundation, set up by American billionaire George Soros, has invested $13 million in Belarus, including $6 million last year mostly for education, ecological amd medical programmes.

The television said that Minsk-based Peter Bern, a U.S. citizen, was accused by the authorities of interfering in Belarus' domestic affairs and was barred "for activities which do not correspond to his status".

It added that Bern was accused of taking part in mass actions organised by the opposition and aired pictures, provided by the KGB security service, showing him watching one of the recent opposition rallies from one side.
"The barring of the opposition's best friend will not mean any difficulties for the Soros Foundation's activities in Belarus," the TV presenter said.
"But lists of the people who have been given grants from this foundation will be published soon and (the Belarussian) people will know who they are," he added.
Bern arrived in Minsk on Sunday afternoon from a meeting in Budapest of the foundation's executive directors from Central and Eastern Europe.

"We intended to meet Bern at the airport but were barred from doing so. They didn't even allow us to talk to him," Roman Yakovlevsky, a Belarussian member of the foundation's management in Minsk, told Reuters. "Bern has been kept at the airport all this time despite some health problems."
Yakovlevsky added that he understood that the authorities would put Bern on a plane to Frankfurt at about 12:30 p.m. (10.30 GMT) on Monday.

"I think the authorities want to adapt the Soros Foundation to the rules established by Belarus's regime," Yakovlevsky said. "We have been under pressure for quite a long time to stop support (in grants) to the independent mass media."

Two American and two German students were briefly detained during protests against hardline President Alexander Lukashenko last Friday. Up to one hundred people were arrested, including at least four opposition leaders.
